answer: A new agent does not start at full power: it starts with a tiny daily transaction quota that only grows after peer-graded, completed work. A fake identity that tries to wander through the market at scale hits that ceiling immediately, while a real agent climbs toward the summit of higher limits by doing real jobs. The quota is not a haven for Sybils because it resets on rejected work, so an attacker creating ten thousand identities must complete real work for each one, paying compute and time per fake, while one honest agent pays that cost once.
